dossier.public_summary: The 2.13-day dip repeats exactly with the star's 2.13-day spot cycle and shows strong out-of-eclipse brightness changes, odd vs even depth differences at 13 sigma and a 499 ppm secondary eclipse. Depths vary by a factor of 4-5 even within the same TESS pipeline and spike during active sectors, which is the fingerprint of a spotted/active star synchronized with the period rather than a planet crossing the star.

reasons.why: Odd and even eclipses differ at 13.8 sigma with 21% depth change, expected for an eclipsing binary folded at twice the true period, not a planet.

Strong secondary eclipse at 0.322 phase with 14.6% of primary depth well above noise, with large phase_curve amplitude 1450 ppm (ratio_to_depth 0.4254 chi2 4890 dof 9) indicates stellar ellipsoidal/spots or close binary, not a planet occultation.

Signal is exactly synchronous with the stellar rotation period measured in all 9 sectors (false_alarm 0.0, amplitude 41754-135840 ppm) with very large phase_curve variation, as expected for spot-modulated variability, not a 2.13 d transiting companion.

Depth changes by 228.7% within the same SPOC 2-min product and transit_depths p_consistent 0.0 with outliers 42.4 sigma show spot-induced depth changes on a variable star, not a constant planet transit.
reasons.value: p_constant 0 changes_within_a_source 0.0 mean_depth_ppm 3240 outlier depths to 12579 ppm

reasons.why: Centroid is on-target ruling out a nearby blended EB with on_target verdict and no plausible neighbour within 1 pixel, so the variable source is the target star itself.
